result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both sheets list all ten signals with exactly the supplied meanings, keep the instructions short, and use dark text on white with no external assets. A's recall section mixes signal-to-meaning and meaning-to-signal prompts over two rounds, so it tests both directions. B only tests meaning to signal, the opposite of the minimum direction the rubric asks for, though its upside-down answer key is a nice touch. Both screenshots are cut off at the bottom, so neither can be confirmed to fit one printed page. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both sheets list all ten signals with the exact meanings and in the original order, and both use a high-contrast look with no external assets. B is better on rubric item 2. Its practice section mixes code-to-meaning and meaning-to-code prompts across two rounds, so it tests both directions. A only asks for the code from the meaning and has no signal-to-meaning practice, though it does add an upside-down answer key. B's two practice rounds run past the bottom of the screenshot, so it's slightly less certain that B fits on one printed page.
